title: Accuracy Guardian Harness for FP8/INT8 Calibration and Gate Automation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement an end-to-end automated accuracy validation harness ("Accuracy Guardian") to validate FP8 and INT8 quantization profiles against FP16 baselines. The harness will run calibrated model variants across a curated 'golden' prompt corpus, compute a multi-dimensional metric suite, enforce pass/fail gates, and produce artifacts that feed into CI, rollout automation, and observability dashboards. Goals: (1) provide deterministic, repeatable acceptance checks for quantized builds; (2) support calibration workflows (per-layer/batch calibration, outlier clipping) and record calibration metadata; (3) expose configurable gating rules per-model and per-deployment; (4) surface drift and adversarial regression signals early.
acceptance_criteria: Harness executes nightly and on PRs for any new quant profile and produces a machine-readable pass/fail artifact.
Gate decision logic integrated with rollout automation: failed runs block canary promotion and mark build as 'quant-failed'.
Calibration metadata (calibration dataset shard, per-layer scales, clip thresholds) are persisted alongside run results and linked in the artifact.
Metric suite (embedding-cosine, normalized log-likelihood delta, token-error-rate, exact-match/top-k recall) is computed and summarized with per-prompt breakdowns.
Artifacts are stored in the designated S3 bucket and a dashboard tile is created (runtime-1.19 / quantization validation panel).
Documentation and runbook for threshold tuning are merged to Confluence and linked from the PR before merge.
Unit and integration tests for the harness runner and comparator are present and green in CI.
updates: 2025-02-03: Kickoff meeting with Product and Applied ML. Scope agreed: FP8 and INT8 profiles, support for per-layer calibration metadata, and baseline FP16 comparator.

2025-02-06: Architecture decision: harness will run in a dedicated CI job using small calibration shards, then rerun full corpus nightly in a batch job. Chose protobuf+parquet for artifacts for compactness and schema evolution.
2025-02-09: Design trade-off: deterministic seed + fixed sampling chosen over stochastic full-sample runs to keep CI runtime under 45m. Agreed to add a periodic stochastic sweep for drift detection.

2025-02-12: Implemented metric collector MVP. Metrics implemented: embedding cosine, average token log-likelihood delta, token-error-rate (TER), top-k recall, and normalized edit distance. Added per-prompt timing telemetry.
2025-02-14: Integration PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/quant-harness/pull/117 — basic runner and comparator. Requesting review from @infra-team and @applied-ml.

2025-02-16: Found an FP8 dynamic-range clipping edgecase on long-context prompts; added a calibration-candidate flag to isolate and rerun with extended clip range. Filed follow-up ENG-84280 for runtime kernel patch.

2025-02-17: PM review feedback: add human-eval anchor set for ambiguous prompts and require at least one human check for any gate that fails by less than 0.5% relative. Incorporating into acceptance criteria.
test_plan: 1) Run harness against small calibration shard (1000 prompts) in CI with FP16 baseline, FP8 and INT8 profiles. Verify run completes <45m.
2) Validate artifacts schema and assert required fields: per-prompt metrics, calibration metadata, deterministic seed, model-tag.
3) Run adversarial perturbation sweep (typos/long-context/truncation) and record sensitivity score per layer.
4) Simulate gating: force a metric regression above threshold and verify canary promotion is blocked and rollback path triggers.
5) Nightly full-corpus run (10k prompts) verifies stability and creates longer-term drift signal.
6) Run human-eval protocol for any run with regression magnitude between 0.25% and 1.0% on primary metric.
risks: False positives from brittle prompts in golden set — mitigation: stratified sampling and human-eval anchor set.
Long CI runtime for large models — mitigation: small-shard PR checks + nightly full runs.
FP8 edgecases causing flaky failures due to kernel numeric limits — mitigation: record calibration metadata and add rerun-with-extended-clip option.
Thresholds misconfigured for customer-facing workloads — mitigation: per-customer profiles and gradual rollout with monitoring.
metrics: Primary pass metric: embedding cosine similarity vs FP16 baseline >= 0.985 (aggregated over golden corpus, mean of per-prompt cosine).
Secondary: average token log-likelihood delta (FP16 - quantized) <= 0.75 nats per token.
Top-1 exact-match decline <= 1.5 percentage points relative to baseline for deterministic tasks.
Per-prompt 95th percentile latency should not exceed baseline 150ms + 50ms overhead for quantized path in the harness environment.
Failure rate (exceptions, timeouts, OOMs) <0.5% across runs. Any OOM must generate an automated issue and attach the calibration metadata.
